Method of Attack: Encrypts data files and executables, renaming encrypted files with gmail email addresses in the filename
Creates a randomly named malware executable in %LocalAppData%\Microsoft Help\
Adds autorun registry entry to start malware on Windows login
Scans all drive letters for data files and executables to encrypt
Does not leave a ransom note
Attack Vector: Unknown initial infection vector; malware installs executable in user AppData and sets autorun registry key
Indicators of Compromise: Encrypted files renamed with pattern originalfilename.extension!___<gmail email>_.crypt, e.g. Tulips.jpg!___prosschiff@gmail.com_.crypt
Malware executable located in C:\Users\User\AppData\Local\Microsoft Help\<random>.exe
Registry entries: HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run\ pointing to the malware executable
